claims.title: Any keychain blob suppresses the API-key fallback, unlike the OpenAI path
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Any keychain blob suppresses the API-key fallback, unlike the OpenAI path**

`hasSubscription` is true for any non-empty string from `readClaudeKeychain()`. It never checks that the entry holds a usable `claudeAiOauth.accessToken`. The OpenAI path is stricter: it only delegates when `auth_mode === "chatgpt"` and an access token exists. Here, a keychain entry that is present but has no OAuth credentials (for example a Claude Code login without a subscription token, or an unparseable blob) causes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to be skipped. The call then falls through to the subscription resolver, which presumably errors or returns an unusable token. Consider parsing the blob and requiring `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` or `refreshToken` before treating it as a subscription, so a stray or empty entry does not block a valid API key. I could not see `resolveAnthropicSubscriptionAuth`, so this depends on how it handles such a blob.

claims.title: Corrupt auth.json with no API key reports "no ~/.codex/auth.json"
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Corrupt auth.json with no API key reports "no ~/.codex/auth.json"**

`!stored` is true both when the file is absent and when it exists but is unparseable. A user with a corrupt `auth.json` and no key is told the file doesn't exist and to run `codex login`. Before this change the failure was a `SyntaxError` that at least pointed at a parse problem. Split the two cases so the message says the file exists but could not be parsed. Both cases here are only reached when `raw` is truthy or falsy, so `raw` can be checked directly.

claims.title: Unparseable auth.json is silently ignored, which can bill the API key with no warning
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Unparseable auth.json is silently ignored, which can bill the API key with no warning**

`parseJsonOrNull` swallows every parse error and returns null with no log. The PR exists to stop a shell `OPENAI_API_KEY` from being billed while a subscription is available. If `~/.codex/auth.json` is corrupted (for example a truncated write during a token rotation) while the user is logged in, `resolveOpenAIAuth` now silently bills `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The user gets no indication that their subscription credentials were skipped. Emit a stderr warning naming the file and the parse error when falling back, so the fallback is visible.

claims.title: Any non-empty keychain string is treated as a usable subscription and blocks the API-key fallback
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Any non-empty keychain string is treated as a usable subscription and blocks the API-key fallback**

`hasSubscription` is truthy for any non-empty string returned by `readClaudeKeychain()`, with no check that it parses or contains a `claudeAiOauth` access/refresh token. If the keychain entry exists but has no usable OAuth block (for example a logged-out state or other data), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is skipped. Control then reaches the subscription path, which will fail. That contradicts the stated rule that the key is used when no subscription credentials exist, and it makes a valid API key unusable. The OpenAI side validates `auth_mode === "chatgpt"` and `access_token`. Apply equivalent validation here.

claims.title: Assertion too weak to prove no fallback to the API key
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Assertion too weak to prove no fallback to the API key**

`.rejects.toThrow()` passes for any error, including unrelated ones such as a typo in the fixture or a missing mock. The test could pass without exercising the refresh-failure path. Assert on the refresh-related error message, and also assert that the result is not an api-key resolution, so it proves the "broken subscription must not silently fall back to the key" invariant.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2cba2c9. `hasClaudeAccessToken` now requires a parseable entry holding a `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` (or top-level `accessToken`); an entry without one falls back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Covered by "falls back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when the keychain entry has no access token".

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2cba2c9. `parseCodexAuth` now distinguishes the cases: a missing file keeps the original "no ~/.codex/auth.json" message, a corrupt one throws "~/.codex/auth.json is not valid JSON — fix or remove it, then run `codex login`".

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2cba2c9. You're right that falling back would undercut the point of the PR. An unparseable auth.json now throws before `OPENAI_API_KEY` is considered, and the same rule applies to the Claude keychain entry (c6c3a55). Tests: "throws instead of billing OPENAI_API_KEY when auth.json is unparseable" and its Anthropic counterpart.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2cba2c9, same change as the sibling thread: the keychain blob must carry an access token to count as a subscription. An unparseable blob now throws instead of being treated as a subscription (c6c3a55), so it can't bill the key silently either.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2cba2c9. The refresh-failure assertions now match `/session expired|refresh failed/i`, and an Anthropic broken-subscription test was added alongside, so neither can pass on an unrelated error.
